meal.title: Default constructor (__init__)
meal.objective: Explain that Python automatically provides a simple __init__ method

voice.script: Hook: What happens when you create an object without writing any setup code? Question: Do I need to write an __init__ method for every class? Concept: Python automatically provides a simple constructor called __init__ that runs whenever an instance is created, even if you never defined one. Code: Here is a class with no __init__ defined, and we create an instance. Execution: When we run the program, it prints the default representation of the object, showing that the hidden __init__ ran. Takeaway: Even without writing one, Python gives each class a basic __init__. Practice: Define a class called Account with no __init__, create an object, and print it.
